source.title: Analysis of a chalcone synthase mutant in Ipomoea purpurea reveals a novel function for flavonoids: amelioration of heat stress

genetic_perturbation.mechanism: Ac/Ds insertion prevents transcription of a functional CHS-D copy; aa plants are white and strongly flavonoid-deficient

design.background_control: two partially inbred lines generated so AA and aa backgrounds were randomized apart from linked loci
design.high_temperature_C: 36 day / 24 night for first 2 weeks, then 32 day / 20 night
design.water_stress_control: humidity and twice-daily saturation watering used to minimize drought confounding

genotype_by_temperature_results.maternal_white_high_temperature_effect: aa recipients approximately 26% lower fertilization success than AA at high temperature; similar at low temperature
genotype_by_temperature_results.paternal_white_high_temperature_effect: aa pollen approximately 24% lower fertilization success than AA on high-temperature recipients; no genotype effect on low-temperature recipients

flower_number.direction: aa produced fewer flowers than AA at low temperature, but the genotypes were similar at high temperature; this endpoint does not show the same white-specific high-temperature disadvantage as fertilization

interpretation: Loss of an early flavonoid-pathway node changes the fitness response to high temperature. The pigment pathway is therefore not merely an output of thermal environment; pathway state also changes thermal performance.
link_to_moricandia: Moricandia provides the complementary causal direction: greater thermal severity under fixed summer photoperiod lowers floral anthocyanin. Together the systems support bidirectional coupling between temperature and pigment-network state.
hard_nonclaims: does not imply high temperature universally favors white flowers; in this experiment high temperature selectively penalizes the CHS-null white genotype
does not imply all white morphs are whole-plant CHS knockouts
does not rescue the failed FCP cross-cohort BIO5 association
published synthesis rather than new raw-data reanalysis
